sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: A very small species, the smallest among those with the finitimus type of enteric valve architecture (EVA); so small that the first specimens were initially taken for individuals from incipient colonies, but a queen with an enlarged abdomen ruled this out. The worker EVA is of the finitimus type, and the workers are among the smallest in the genus (hind tibia length WT3L = 1.12–1.20 mm), their enteric valve also the smallest in the genus. The soldier is among the smallest in the genus (head length SHdL = 2.42–2.66 mm), comparable to the smallest I. fungifaber, but with the finitimus type of EVA; the mandibles are evenly curved, the acceleration index of mandible curvature between the proximal and distal parts very low (ln(SMlpR) − ln(SMldR) = 0.96–1.44), similar to some I. planifrons individuals, but the body size differs. The alate is medium-sized within the genus, closest to the alates of I. finitimus, I. rectimalatus and I. planifrons. It is at present known only from the forêt des Abeilles in Gabon.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule well sclerotized and dark (C6–C7); frontal gland pore concolorous with the head capsule; postclypeus one shade paler than the head capsule; antennae C5–C6. Pronotum concolorous or almost concolorous with the head capsule; meso- and metanotum C6, slightly paler than the head; legs C4; abdominal tergites C6; sternites distinctly paler in the middle (C3–C5) and darker at the sides (C5–C6), and darker than the anterior ones. Head capsule with conspicuous setae scattered among the dense short fine hairs forming the felt; labrum and postclypeus with conspicuous setae mixed with short hairs; antennae with conspicuous setae and more numerous small hairs, most segments with a tuft of very fine curved hairs at the tip (visible above 50×). Pronotum setae mainly on the margins, shorter in the middle; meso- and metanotum with fine pale hairs arranged along the median band (generally visible at 20–40×), the posterior lobe sometimes with 1–2 large setae. Legs hairy, the fore coxa with 7–11 stronger setae on the ridge, 1–3 on the ventral surface of the fore coxa and trochanter; fore, mid and hind tibiae with 3, 2 and 2 apical spurs and 0, 2 and 0 subapical spurs respectively, each tibia with 30–40 spines. Abdominal tergites with setae of mixed sizes; sternites with long setae erect or slightly inclined forward, together with many long and small setae directed posteriorly. Compound eyes nearly circular; ocelli short-oval, separated from the compound eye by about 0.9–1.3 times the small ocellar diameter; frontal gland pore generally a small circular or elongate mark. Antennae reduced to 12 segments in the queen and male through breakage (about 4 segments lost). Labrum domed, wider than long. Left mandible apical tooth medium-sized within the genus, always more prominent than the first marginal tooth; 3 marginal teeth, the second expressed only as an undulation of the tooth margin between the first and third; only the apical tooth sharp in unworn specimens; the premolar almost completely hidden by the molar prominence in dorsal view; the dorsal surface of the molar with a rounded molar prominence ending posteriorly in a small sharp process. Right mandible apical tooth always more prominent than the first marginal tooth; 2 marginal teeth, the first sharp-tipped when fresh, the second smaller and blunt-tipped even when fresh; the molar with a rounded labial process ventrally and heel-shaped posteriorly. Pronotum distinctly wider than long, narrower than the head width (including compound eyes), flat to very weakly saddle-shaped, the anterior lobe short and very slightly raised; the fore coxa with a lip-like projection ventrally forming a sharp ridge. Gut not studied. Measurements: compound eye major diameter 0.41–0.46 mm, head width including compound eyes 1.56–1.65 mm, distance from the apical tooth to the first marginal tooth 0.21–0.24 mm, ocellus major diameter 0.15–0.18 mm, postclypeus width 0.77–0.82 mm, pronotum width 1.38–1.48 mm.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule uniformly C5; antennae and labrum 1–2 shades paler than the head capsule; mandibles dark (C6), the base abruptly one shade paler, generally concolorous with the frons; thorax and legs paler than the head capsule (C4); abdomen grey to red-brown from the gut contents. Head capsule with a few scattered setae; a dense tuft of hairs on the frons surrounds and covers the frontal gland pore; antennae with conspicuous setae and more numerous small hairs, the apical segment with a tuft of very fine curved hairs at its tip (visible above 50×); the labrum with 4–6 large setae on each lateral lobe; pronotum and mesonotum with few setae, mainly on the margins. Fore coxa with at least 1 fine seta, 2–3 spines on the ridge and no spines ventrally; trochanter generally with stout setae in a row, including 3–4 spines; fore, mid and hind tibiae with 3, 2 and 2 apical spurs and 0, 2 and 0 subapical spurs respectively (the latter sometimes weak), each tibia with a row of 6–12 spines. Abdominal tergites with the large setae mainly or only on the posterior margin; sternites with long setae erect or slightly inclined forward, often pigmented, together with small setae directed posteriorly. The soldier is among the smallest within the genus. Head capsule distinctly sclerotized, distinctly longer than wide; in dorsal view the sides mostly nearly parallel, very slightly narrowing in the posterior 1/3–1/4, converging from the antennal sockets towards the mandible bases, the posterior margin regularly convex; the upper margin slightly concave or straight; the angle between the protruding mandibles and the frons obtuse; the frons flat or with a small anterior swelling. Gulamentum in ventral view narrowing in the posterior half, the anterior half rounded and convex at the sides. Antennae 14.5–15 segmented. Labrum always deeply forked, wider than long, the sides harp-shaped; the lobes angular, their tips fine, white or semitransparent; the anterior margin concave. Mandibles sabre-like, distinctly shorter than the head, the inner margin smooth, each with 1 distinct but small marginal tooth near the molar area; the surface of both smooth and shining; the right mandible slightly more curved than the left. Pronotum saddle-shaped, 56%–60% of the head width, the anterior and posterior margins straight; the fore coxa with a lip-like projection ventrally forming a sharp ridge. Enteric valve inserted on the left side, best seen in ventral view, in the posterior half of the abdomen. Caecum small, best seen in ventral view, near the middle of the abdomen, with 3 lobes. Enteric valve primary cushions (PC) arranged with trigonal symmetry, the odd cushion recognizable as the finitimus type of EVA. Measurements: head dorsal concavity sagitta 0.00–0.05 mm, head length 2.42–2.66 mm, head width 1.80–1.89 mm, left mandible ventral length 1.93–2.16 mm, left mandible minor curvature 0.22–0.26 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule pale (C2–C3); proximal antennal segments pale (C2), the apical segment two shades darker (C4); thorax, tergites and legs pale (C2–C3); abdomen grey to red-brown from the gut contents. Head capsule and postclypeus with a few scattered erect setae; labrum with a few scattered stout setae; antennae with conspicuous setae and more numerous small hairs, the apical segment with a tuft of fine curved hairs at its tip (visible above 50×); thoracic tergites with scattered setae. Fore coxa ridged, with 1 fine seta, 3–5 spines on the ridge and no spines ventrally; fore trochanter with 4–6 spines in a row; fore, mid and hind tibiae with 3, 2 and 2 apical spurs and 0, 2 and 0 subapical spurs respectively, and with a row of 6–12 spines. Abdominal tergites with scattered setae; sternites with long setae erect or slightly inclined forward, often pigmented, together with small setae directed posteriorly. The worker is the smallest among the species with the finitimus type of EVA, as small as the smallest workers of I. fungifaber (which has the fungifaber type of EVA) (WT3L = 1.12–1.20 mm). Head capsule weakly sclerotized (except the mandibles). Antennae 14.5 segmented. Labrum domed. Left mandible apical tooth well developed, sharp-tipped when fresh; 3 marginal teeth, the first well developed but blunt-tipped even when fresh, the second weak (expressed only as an undulating tooth margin, disappearing with wear), the third blunt-tipped; the proximal premolar generally hidden by the molar prominence; the dorsal surface of the molar with a rounded molar prominence ending posteriorly in a small sharp process. Right mandible apical tooth well developed, sharp when fresh; 2 marginal teeth, the first well developed and sharp when fresh, the second smaller and blunt-tipped even when fresh; the molar with a rounded labial process ventrally and heel-shaped posteriorly. Pronotum saddle-shaped, about 64% of the head width; the fore coxa with a lip-like projection ventrally forming a sharp ridge. Enteric valve inserted on the left side, best seen in ventral view, in the posterior half of the abdomen. Enteric valve primary cushions of the finitimus type, with trigonal symmetry: the downstream part of the odd cushion is broad, its bulbous inflation bearing very dense shorter setae; supporting setae rather numerous, 20–28 on each side of the odd cushion; secondary cushions broad upstream, distinctly narrowing downstream, the spines evenly distributed. Caecum always small, visible in ventral view, near the middle of the abdomen, with short lobes (3–4 small lobes). Measurements: maximum head width 1.07–1.13 mm, distance from the left mandible apical tooth to the first marginal tooth 0.17–0.18 mm, left mandible functional length 0.52–0.57 mm, mean length of primary cushions 1–6 0.45–0.48 mm, mean width 0.06–0.08 mm, mean length of secondary cushions 0.36–0.39 mm, mean width 0.16–0.22 mm, odd primary cushion elongation index WVPOdd-Elg = 4.85–7.20.
